brief: Climate talks collapsed and the PABS pandemic-annex deadline slipped, so the next six weeks are about elections and EU money rather than new health treaties. My main view is that there is no special World Health Assembly in December. WHO's 13 November line was that members still aim to finish the PABS annex by May 2027, so the 14–15 December session is very unlikely to happen. Spain votes on 29 November, and I expect a PP plurality and a PP-Vox majority. I put Chiang Wan-an at about 88% in Taipei, well above the crowd's 70%. The crowd's 90% for Feijóo as 'next PM' by 30 November looks mis-timed, because Spanish government formation takes weeks. I also think the 24% for a US screwworm national emergency is too high.

events.title: Tweede Kamer — commissiedebat EU-Gezondheidsraad
events.expect: The committee debate goes ahead and prepares the Dutch line for the 8 December EPSCO Health Council. MPs will probably file motions in a follow-up two-minute debate before EPSCO. I haven't verified the agenda; this is based on Dutch parliamentary routine.

events.watch: Rescheduling by the Kamer's agenda committee, or a cabinet-related disruption.

events.title: Special European Council on the MFF 2028–2034
events.expect: No final MFF deal. Special summits on the long-term budget have historically ended without agreement at the first attempt. I expect a negotiating-box-style discussion, with frugal states and cohesion/farm-funding recipients still far apart. Health spending lines are unlikely to be settled.

events.watch: Summit extended past 27 November, or a leaked revised negotiating box with figures.

events.title: Palestine — legislative election
events.expect: Real doubt that it happens on schedule. I did not verify preparations, and no market is trading on it. If it is held, expect voting in the West Bank only, with Gaza excluded or impractical and Hamas's participation contested. Treat this as close to a coin flip.

events.watch: An official postponement notice or a Central Elections Commission statement on polling stations.

events.title: Taiwan — local elections (nine-in-one)
events.expect: KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an holds Taipei comfortably. The KMT should again win more of the 22 city and county top posts than the DPP. I put Chiang well above the crowd's 70%.

calls.q: Chiang Wan-an wins the Taipei mayoral election
The KMT wins more of the 22 mayor and county-magistrate posts than the DPP

events.watch: Late Taipei polls showing the DPP within 5 points, or a sharp turnout swing.

events.title: Spain — snap general election
events.expect: All four polls published on 22 November put PP first, and PP plus Vox at 190–210 seats against 176 needed. I expect Feijóo to become PM, but not by 30 November, because investiture takes weeks. This matters for the PP-Vox health and migration agenda.

calls.q: The PP wins the most seats in Spain's 29 November general election
PP and Vox together win at least 176 of 350 seats
Vox wins at least 60 seats

events.watch: A PSOE rise past 30% in final polls, or Vox falling below 17%.

events.title: IGWG — reserved dates for further PABS annex meetings (as needed)
events.expect: The reserved dates probably go unused. WHO's 13 November news item says members reiterated commitment to finalise the PABS annex by May 2027. That points to continued talks into 2027 rather than an emergency December round.

calls.q: The IGWG holds a formal PABS negotiating session between 30 November and 4 December 2026

events.watch: A WHO notice convening IGWG for these dates or co-chairs announcing a breakthrough.

events.title: The Gambia — presidential election
events.expect: Incumbent Adama Barrow is the favourite against a split opposition under a first-past-the-post system, so there is no runoff. I did not search for recent polling, so I hold some uncertainty on margin. A win above 50% is likely but not certain.

calls.q: Adama Barrow is declared winner of The Gambia's presidential election
Barrow wins more than 50% of the valid vote

events.watch: Opposition consolidation behind one candidate, or electoral commission delays.

events.title: 5th Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR
events.expect: The conference should close with a ministerial outcome document, following the Jeddah precedent of 2024. Expect commitments on surveillance, financing and the evidence panel on AMR, but little in binding or funded terms. The Africa venue should push manufacturing and access language.

events.watch: Delegation downgrades, or a draft text circulating without finance or accountability language.

events.title: EPSCO Council (Health)
events.expect: The meeting goes ahead under the Irish presidency. I have not verified the agenda, so expect routine progress reports and possibly one health file reaching a Council position. Do not expect headline decisions.

calls.q: The EPSCO Council (Health) meets in Brussels on 8 December 2026
The Council agrees a general approach or Council negotiating position on at least one health legislative file at the meeting

events.watch: The published provisional agenda showing 'general approach' items.

events.title: Haiti — general election, first round (with constitutional referendum)
events.expect: I doubt the vote happens on the date. Gang control of much of the country and repeated slippage of earlier dates make another delay more likely than not. If held, expect very low turnout and a partial, disputed process.

calls.q: Haiti's general election first round is held on 13 December 2026

events.watch: Electoral council confirming ballot printing and distribution, or a security-driven postponement.

events.title: G20 Leaders' Summit
events.expect: Trump hosts, and the US has pared the agenda back, so a long consensus communiqué is a coin flip at best. Health and pandemic language is unlikely in any joint text. Xi's attendance is uncertain after Shenzhen.

calls.q: Donald Trump attends the G20 Leaders' Summit in Miami in person
G20 leaders adopt a joint leaders' declaration by 16 December 2026
Any joint G20 leaders' text refers to health or pandemic preparedness

events.watch: Sherpa-level reports on a declaration versus a chair's summary; Chinese attendance announcements.

events.title: Possible special session of the WHA to adopt the PABS annex
events.expect: Very unlikely to happen. The IGWG did not deliver an agreed text, the Executive Board's 13 November deadline to call a special session has passed, and WHO's 13 November item points to May 2027. I expect the PABS annex to go to WHA80.

events.watch: Any WHO notice convening delegates in Geneva for 14–15 December.

events.expect: Another postponement is much more likely than voting. I did not verify current preparations, but the political settlement is fragile and the conditions for a credible vote look weak. I'd expect an announced delay close to the date.
